task.description: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-001b.md independently. Run WF-02 Step 1b's gate: (a) every acceptance criterion has a corresponding design element, no TBD/deferral language outside the explicitly-labeled open-questions section; (b) props/types (here: message-catalog key names, not component props, since this requirement adds no new component) fully specified; (c) no color/spacing/token violation — this requirement touches no CSS, so this check is trivially satisfied, confirm the design doesn't introduce any; (d) no .tsx implementation code present. The design makes several judgment calls you must specifically evaluate: (1) all 12 components correctly identified as Server Components using getTranslations — verify by reading the actual files' first lines yourself; (2) the flat-indexed-key vs JSON-array-value decision for the 6 repeated-shape arrays (Events.TALKS, MapSection.CHAPTERS, Metrics.METRICS, Partners.PARTNERS, Streams.STREAMS, Team.TEAM) — the design picked flat indexed keys and flagged it as open question 4 needing your confirmation; give an actual verdict, don't just note it's flagged. (3) The empty-array-copy pitfall audit (content_ba_guide.md §5) — verify the design's claim that none of the 12 components uses array.join()-into-a-sentence by checking the actual source yourself. Six open questions are listed (brand-name extraction scope, <em>-emphasis handling, Telegram-handle splitting, flat-key-vs-array choice, MapSection aria-label desync, nav anchor scope) — for each, decide whether it's a legitimate implementation-time judgment call to leave for FRONTEND-DEV, or something that must be resolved before Step 2 can proceed sensibly.
acceptance_criteria: Checks a-d run against docs/agents/design/REQ-001b.md directly
Server/Client component classification independently verified against actual source files
A real verdict given on the flat-key-vs-JSON-array open question, not just acknowledgment that it's flagged
Each of the 6 open questions explicitly triaged: pass-through to FRONTEND-DEV, or blocking

result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-001b.md directly, independent of the handoff's characterization of it. All four gate checks pass: (a) all 5 REQ-001b acceptance criteria (requirements.yaml lines 128-132) map to concrete design elements in SS5's table, verified against SS1-SS4's actual content, not just the table's own claims; no TBD/deferral language found anywhere outside the explicitly labeled SS4 open-questions section (grepped). (b) SS2's per-component key table gives fully field-level flat key names for every one of the 12 namespaces (e.g. principle1Title/principle1Body, not vague placeholders) -- cross-checked exhaustively against the actual source strings in all 12 files. (c) No color/hex/spacing/token content anywhere in the design; the one CSS-adjacent item (statusClass) is correctly kept as a non-extracted literal, so zero token surface is touched, as expected for a copy-only requirement. (d) No .tsx code blocks present -- confirmed no code fences in the file at all. Independently re-verified the design's two load-bearing factual claims against real source: read all 12 landing component files' opening lines myself (Band, Creed, Doors, Events, Footer, Hero, MapSection, Metrics, Nav, Partners, Streams, Team) -- none has a "use client" directive, confirming the Server-Component/getTranslations claim for all 12. Also read the six components with data arrays (Events.TALKS, MapSection.CHAPTERS, Metrics.METRICS, Partners.PARTNERS, Streams.STREAMS, Team.TEAM) in full -- confirmed none uses array.join() or any array-to-sentence interpolation; all six render one repeated DOM block per item via .map(), matching the design's claim. Checked next-intl's actual shipped types (node_modules/use-intl/dist/types/core/AbstractIntlMessages.d.ts, createTranslator.d.ts, TranslationValues.d.ts, createFormatter.d.ts) rather than taking the design's characterization on faith: AbstractIntlMessages is typed as `{[id: string]: AbstractIntlMessages | string}` -- nested string leaves only, no array variant in the type -- confirming flat indexed keys is the only pattern next-intl's typed message shape and t()/t.rich() resolution model actually support; a JSON-array-valued entry would require t.raw() (returns `any`, an untyped escape hatch) and would bypass ICU interpolation and t.rich() entirely. Verdict on open question 4: CONFIRM flat indexed keys (option a) as designed -- it is the only pattern the library's own types support as first-class, not merely the more conservative choice. Also confirmed t.rich() exists (RichTagsFunction-based) and format.list() exists (ICU/Intl.ListFormatOptions-based array-to-sentence formatting) -- next-intl's actual supported mechanism for joining an array into a sentence, which the 12 components correctly never use, reinforcing the SS3 pitfall-audit finding. Triage of all 6 SS4 open questions: (1) brand-name extraction scope -- SAFE PASS-THROUGH to FRONTEND-DEV; either choice (extract 'AI Qadam' as a key or leave it literal like the non-copy URLs) is mechanically reversible and affects zero visible behavior or acceptance criteria either way, recommend leaving it literal per content_ba_guide.md's 'no permitted variants' framing but not blocking on it. (2) <em>-emphasis handling -- SAFE PASS-THROUGH, now with concrete direction: next-intl's t.rich() is confirmed to exist and is exactly the documented mechanism for this (verified in createTranslator.d.ts), so FRONTEND-DEV should use t.rich() with a tag-function value for the em span rather than dangerouslySetInnerHTML or manual string splitting; this is an implementation-pattern choice, not a content or catalog-shape decision, so it does not need to come back to design. (3) Telegram-handle splitting -- SAFE PASS-THROUGH, genuinely cosmetic (one key vs. two for an invariant token), zero effect on acceptance criteria or catalog structure either way. (4) flat-key-vs-array -- RESOLVED by this gate, not a pass-through: confirmed flat indexed keys per the verdict above, FRONTEND-DEV should treat this as decided, not still open. (5) MapSection aria-label desync -- SAFE PASS-THROUGH, explicitly out of scope: the design correctly identifies this as a pre-existing latent risk this requirement neither introduces nor is positioned to fix (fixing it would mean deriving the aria-label from CHAPTERS programmatically, which is a structural change beyond copy extraction) -- correctly left for a future requirement, not a Step-2 blocker. (6) nav anchor scope -- NOT REALLY OPEN: the design already states affirmatively, backed by a direct Nav.tsx read, that anchors do not change; this is confirmed correct and should be treated as closed, not left open for FRONTEND-DEV to re-litigate.
